newsitem.title: UK: London gold totters lower as negative thinking grows.
newsitem.headline: London gold totters lower as negative thinking grows.

text.p: Gold prices were tottering on the verge of fresh recent lows after the bearish sentiment of last week swept through the markets again on Monday, dealers said.

Rumoured selling by South African and Australian gold miners as they became increasingly anxious to protect their income against falling prices was cited as a major factor eroding the value of gold and the market's confidence.
But also playing on already fraying nerves was fresh rumour that a central bank had sold bullion out of its gold reserves.
"There has been a continual drip of metal on the market. It's been disappointing that the price is at a 20-month low at a time when it is traditionally high," a dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $370.50 per ounce after $371.30 on Friday putting the market's current value a matter of pennies above its fixing on April 25, 1994 when bullion was fixed at $370.25.
"There was an attempt to sell it down through the key $370.00 support already this morning. Now there is a good chance of a short-covering bounce to around $372.00," a dealer said.
He added, "It's vulnerable longer term though. The mood is pretty negative."
A key factor in the gold price's short-term movement will be what happens in New York when the U.S. markets re-open after their two-day Thanksgiving holiday.
The spot gold price was around $373.50 when the U.S. markets finished for their break last Wednesday.
"It is quite far away from where it was when New York left for Thanksgiving. New York hasn't really been involved at these lower levels yet," a dealer said.
There was a chance that dealers who were positioned for the price falling when New York reopens on Monday, might decide to buy metal to hedge their bets, the dealer said.
However undermining dealers' position taking was the more significant maneouvring of gold producers anxious to protect their profit markgins in a falling market.

"If you look at the Australian dollar (price), it's down to A$451. Producers are going to have to sell the stuff and the further down the gold price goes the more pressure is on them," a dealer based in continental Europe said.
"They're not going to wait until it gets to A$400. "The same is true with the (South African) rand. For the last 15 days we've seen gold sold by producers," he added.
Tradionally gold demand reaches its peak between November and February as the jewellery makers buy gold to provide for Christmas shopping in the west.
This coincides with the end of the monsoons, the Indian wedding season and the other major festivals in the gold-affinity countries of Asia.
The Chinese new year traditionally gives another boost to jewellery buying which feeds back into the bullion market.
However this year as bullion prices eroded, the jewellers and other physical buyers have been more cagey, dealers said.
"There was good physical demand at around $375.00. Now they seem to be waiting for lower prices," a dealer said.
According to technical analysts who study charts of past prices to forecast future trends, the pattern suggests supportive buying for gold can be expected.

"Our downside target -- $370 for spot -- has now been fulfilled and with the market oversold, historic support immediately below this level should hold," said techncial analyst Elli Gifford at Investment Reaearch of Cambridge.
Dealers said that could mean a fall to $365 or even lower before the buyers come back in numbers.
"This market is heading for $360. That's the view on this desk anyway," said one London-based dealer.
The other precious metals were taken up with the mood in the gold market.
Platinum fixed at a fresh three-year low of $373.75 down from $374.50 on Friday and silver was precariously a couple of cents above key key support at $4.72/$4.74.
Palladium however was a little firmer at $114.509/$115.50, about 25 cents up from Friday's close. REUTERS bs
